title: Add pre-decision expectation-vs-observation discrepancy check (surprise cues) alongside Active Mind

sections.what: Add a pre-decision appraisal step that compares incoming third-party observations and room changes against the character's Active Mind assumptions and obligations, surfacing prediction-error/surprise cues when reality contradicts expectations.
sections.why: task-944 defines Active Mind constructs (questions, assumptions, obligations) and invalidates assumptions when a character's own action fails (empty pocket). However, there is no pre-decision discrepancy comparison for incoming third-party actions, arrivals, revealed weapons, or broken commitments - leaving sudden surprises unflagged unless already caught as generic danger.
sections.how: 1. Add a deterministic discrepancy evaluator comparing Active Mind entries (active_mind.assumptions, obligations, open questions) and baseline entity expectations against current room snapshot / recent_hearing / turn_events (missing expected companion, breached door, unexpected armed posture or betrayal by trusted acquaintance).\n2. Surface matched discrepancies as concise prediction-error / surprise cues into Intermediator (task-948) and turn cognition (task-944) alongside a proportional surprise emotion spike in engine/emotion.py.\n3. Keep the check strictly grounded in current observed state and prior character state (zero omniscient script/narrative knowledge).
sections.verify: 1. Run pytest and JS unit tests covering discrepancy detection between Active Mind assumptions/obligations and observed room/turn events, asserting surprise cue emission and zero false positives when observations align.

acceptance.text: Before cognition/decision, incoming observations (third-party arrivals, violent/armed turn events, speech, and violated obligations) are compared against the character's Active Mind assumptions, obligations, and expectations.
Detects mismatches deterministically (without story-director scripting) to emit an explicit surprise/discrepancy perception cue and optional surprise affect spike into turn cognition.
Unit tests verify both expectation confirmation (zero discrepancy) and violation (unexpected violence/missing ally/contradicted assumption) paths cleanly.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Agent Turn Modal prompt context (`=== ACTIVE MIND ===` / sensory surprise cue) and Intermediator synthesis input.

Current availability: task-944 models Active Mind invalidation only when a character's own action fails (e.g. checking an empty pocket), with no incoming third-party expectation-vs-observation appraisal.

Manual verification steps:
1. Seed a character with an Active Mind assumption or obligation (e.g. believing an ally is safe/unarmed or expected in an area).
2. Inject a contradicting third-party observation (missing ally, weapon revealed, hostile speech/action) and inspect the pre-decision prompt / affect delta.
   - expected: A concise prediction-error discrepancy cue surfaces in cognition and spikes surprise attention.
